Purpose To examined the time-course of the early and late phase of the rate of voluntary force development (RVFD) and muscle damage markers after downhill running. Methods Ten recreational runners performed a 30-min downhill run at 10 km h −1 and −20% (−11.3°) on a motorized treadmill. At baseline and each day up to 4 days RVFD, knee extensors maximum voluntary isometric force (MVIC), serum creatine kinase (CK) concentration, quadriceps swelling, and soreness were assessed. The early (0–50 ms) and late (100–200 ms) phase of the RVFD, as well as the force developed at 50 and 200 ms, were also determined. Results MVIC showed moderate decrements (p < 0.05) and recovered after 4 days (p > 0.05). Force at 50 ms and the early phase were not impaired (p > 0.05). Conversely, force at 200 ms and the late phase showed moderate decrements (p < 0.05) and recovered after 3 and 4 days, respectively (p > 0.05). CK concentration, quadriceps swelling, and soreness increased (p < 0.05) were overall fully resolved after 4 days (p > 0.05). Conclusion Downhill running affected the knee extensors RVFD late but not early phase. The RVFD late phase may be used as an additional marker of muscle damage in trail running. Keywords Creatine kinase Delayed onset muscle soreness Eccentric Maximum voluntary contraction Muscle swelling Musculoskeletal Quadriceps Trail running Ultra-Endurance Sports Science & Medicine Università degli Studi di Milano Open access funding provided by Università degli Studi di Milano within the CRUI-CARE Agreement. issue-copyright-statement © Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2024 Introduction Performing eccentric exercise is known to induce symptoms of muscle damage (Clarkson and Hubal 2002 ). Decreased force, as well as increased muscle soreness, swelling and/or muscle protein activity are among the most common indicators used to monitor the reparation process taking place the days following the eccentric session (Nosaka and Clarkson 1995 ). However, they manifest with an unsynchronized time-course after the eccentric exercise. Interestingly, eccentric exercise can be performed in different modalities, and muscle damage has been investigated using dynamic constant external load or isokinetic device (Coratella and Bertinato 2015 ), flywheel instruments (Coratella et al. 2016 ), eccentric cycling (Peñailillo et al. 2015 ; Mavropalias et al. 2020 ), and downhill running (Byrnes et al. 1985 ; Khassetarash et al. 2021 ). Particularly, downhill running places unique biomechanical, neuromuscular, and physiological challenges on the human body (Giandolini et al. 2016 ; Vernillo et al. 2017 , 2020 ; Bontemps et al. 2020 ; Khassetarash et al. 2020 , 2021 ). Therefore, it has raised a scientific interest given the increasing participation in trail and ultratrail running (Hoffman et al. 2010 ), whose downhill running seems to be a crucial aspect of the performance (Bontemps et al. 2020 ). Using downhill running as an eccentric exercise model could (i) inform aspects of training preparation in trail and ultratrail events, and (ii) minimize the risk of overuse injuries associated with greater impact loading and muscle damage. While maximal force is generally considered as the gold standard to evaluate global changes in neuromuscular function, it was recently suggested that this evaluation may be incomplete, and the rise in muscle force should also be considered for a more comprehensive evaluation (Maffiuletti et al. 2016 ). Although instantaneous force values at specific time points could provide further insights, the rate of voluntary force development (RVFD) has been more recently adopted for a more comprehensive evaluation of a task-induced neuromuscular changes (D’Emanuele et al. 2021 ). The RVFD denotes the ability of the neuromuscular system to rapidly increase force over time (e.g., usually in the first 200–250 ms) (Maffiuletti et al. 2016 ). Specifically, the slope from the first 50–100 ms of the force–time curve has been described as the early phase, and mainly depends on neural aspects such as the firing of the motor units for the muscles involved in the task (Del Vecchio et al. 2019 ). In contrast, the slope from 100 to 250 ms has been described as the late phase, and depends on a series of structural factors such as muscle morphology (Aagaard et al. 2002 ), muscle architecture (Coratella et al. 2020 ), and tendon stiffness (Maffiuletti et al. 2016 ). Muscle damage is initiated by a disruption of the sarcomeres and an impairment in the excitation–contraction coupling (Proske and Morgan 2001 ). Both mechanisms may have implications on the RVFD, specifically on its late phase since they refer to the muscle structure instead of the neural component. After an eccentric cycling bout for 30 min at 60% of maximal concentric power output, Peñailillo et al. ( 2015 ) showed that RVFD can be considered an indirect marker of eccentric exercise-induced muscle damage. However, several physiological and biomechanical differences between running and cycling exist (Millet et al. 2009 ), so whether or not the RVFD may present the same behaviour after downhill running remains to be investigated. In addition, Peñailillo et al. ( 2015 ) stopped the examination at 48 h after the eccentric protocol, while it is known that muscle damage may last much further (Clarkson and Hubal 2002 ). Therefore, the present study aimed to examine the time-course alterations of the early and late phase of RVFD induced by a session of downhill running, together with other traditional muscle damage markers. This information could be of practical significance in trail running and following prolonged duration races wherein cumulative downhill eccentric loading is high.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-course alterations of early and late phases of the rate of voluntary force development (RVFD) and traditional muscle damage markers following a 30-minute downhill running session in recreational runners. It concluded that downhill running impairs the RVFD late phase, maximal voluntary isometric force (MVIC), serum creatine kinase (CK), quadriceps swelling, and muscle soreness for up to 72 hours, with full recovery generally observed within 4 days, while the early phase of RVFD remains unaffected. The RVFD late phase is suggested as an additional sensitive marker of eccentric-induced muscle damage in trail running.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 30-minute downhill run was performed at 10 km/h with a -20% (-11.3°) decline on a motorized treadmill. Effects were monitored for up to 4 days, with full recovery generally observed by day 4. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Moderate decrements (p < 0.05), specifically lower at POST24 (84   ± 13% of PRE values) and POST72 (90   ± 13% of PRE values) compared to PRE, fully recovered after 4 days (p > 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents the maximal force-generating capacity and strength production of a muscle group.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-downhill running session (up to 72 hours post-bout), recovering within 4 days.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle damage and impaired maximal voluntary force production and neuromuscular function.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Force at 50 ms (Early phase of RVFD)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not impaired; did not show a time effect (p > 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects initial rapid force generation capacity and neural aspects of muscle activation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-downhill running assessment (up to 96 hours post-bout).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates no significant impairment in the early neural activation or rapid force generation capacity of muscle following downhill running.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Rate of voluntary force development (slope of force-time curve)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not impaired (p > 0.05); no significant difference detected when compared to PRE values (all p = 1.000).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects initial rapid neural drive and muscle activation, primarily depending on the firing of motor units.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-downhill running session (up to 96 hours post-bout).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Not sensitive to eccentric-induced muscle damage, indicating that early neural aspects of force development are preserved.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Force at 200 ms (Late phase of RVFD)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Moderate decrements (p < 0.05), specifically lower at POST48 (83   ± 20% of PRE values), recovering after 3 days (p > 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects sustained force generation capacity and structural factors of muscle, such as morphology, architecture, and tendon stiffness.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-downhill running session (impaired up to 48 hours post-bout).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates impairment in the muscle's ability to rapidly produce sustained force, linked to structural muscle damage.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Rate of voluntary force development (slope of force-time curve, neuromuscular performance measure)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Moderately decremented (p < 0.05), remaining lower until POST72 (74   ± 31% of PRE values), and recovering after 4 days (p > 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects structural factors of muscle (e.g., morphology, architecture, tendon stiffness, type-II fibres, Ca2+ release, cross-bridge formation rates), initiated by sarcomere disruption and impairment in excitation-contraction coupling.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-downhill running session (impaired for up to 72 hours).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Sensitive to eccentric-induced muscle damage, indicating impairment in rapid force production capacity due to muscle structure rather than neural components; may serve as an additional muscle damage marker in trail running.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly (p < 0.05), peaking at POST24 (613   ± 394% of PRE values), remaining elevated at POST48 (232   ± 118% of PRE values), and fully resolved after 4 days (p > 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An enzyme released into the bloodstream from damaged muscle cells, indicating muscle fiber damage and disruption of myonuclei.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-downhill running session (peaked at 24 hours, elevated up to 48 hours post-bout).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A traditional and classic biochemical indicator confirming muscle fiber damage due to eccentric exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly (p < 0.05), specifically higher at POST24 (102   ± 1% of PRE values) and remaining higher until POST72 (102   ± 2% of PRE values), fully resolved after 4 days (p > 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents localized fluid accumulation in muscle tissue (edema), indicating inflammation and cellular damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-downhill running session (up to 72 hours post-bout).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A physical indicator confirming muscle damage and inflammatory response following eccentric exercise.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Subjective symptom measurement (Pressure pain threshold assessment)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly (p < 0.05), with decreased pressure pain threshold observed at POST48 (77   ± 27% of PRE values) and POST72 (81   ± 18% of PRE values), fully resolved after 4 days (p > 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Perceived discomfort, pain, and tenderness in muscles, typically associated with delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) and inflammation following strenuous eccentric exercise.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-downhill running session (peaked between 48 and 72 hours post-bout).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A subjective indicator confirming muscle damage, inflammation, and recovery status from eccentric exercise.
